questions.question: Which vessels branch off the aorta first?
questions.explain: The coronary arteries leave the aortic root just above the valve cusps, so the heart muscle is supplied before any other organ.

questions.question: Which chamber has the thickest wall?
questions.explain: The left ventricle pumps against systemic pressure, so its wall is roughly 8–12 mm thick, about three times the right ventricle's.

questions.question: How many leaflets does the mitral valve have?
questions.explain: The mitral valve has an anterior and a posterior leaflet, held shut by chordae tendineae and papillary muscles.

questions.question: What makes the first heart sound (S1)?
questions.explain: S1 is the closure of the inlet valves at the start of ventricular contraction.

questions.question: Where is the heart's natural pacemaker?
questions.explain: The sinoatrial node sits high in the right atrium and fires at 60–100 bpm at rest.

questions.question: Why does the AV node delay the signal?
options: To let the atria finish emptying
questions.explain: The roughly 0.1 s delay lets atrial contraction finish before the ventricles start, so filling is complete.

questions.question: When does most left ventricular coronary flow happen?
questions.explain: During systole the contracting muscle squeezes its own vessels shut, so most left ventricular perfusion happens in diastole.

questions.question: What does the Frank-Starling law describe?
options: More filling stretch means a stronger contraction
questions.explain: Within limits, greater filling stretches the muscle and increases the force of the next contraction.

questions.question: Ejection fraction is the share of which volume that is ejected?
questions.explain: Ejection fraction is stroke volume divided by end-diastolic volume, normally about 55–70%.

questions.question: Why does an oral substance reach the heart after the liver?
options: The liver lies in the chest
Portal blood drains to the liver before the vena cava
The heart pumps it to the liver first
questions.explain: Blood from the gut drains through the portal vein into the liver, then leaves by the hepatic veins to the inferior vena cava.

questions.question: How wide are capillaries compared with a red blood cell?
questions.explain: Capillaries are 5–10 µm and red cells 7–8 µm, so cells deform to pass through single file.

questions.question: A beta-blocker mainly does what to the heart?
questions.explain: Blocking beta-1 receptors reduces both heart rate and contractility, lowering oxygen demand.
